Stated Claim / Post Context:
Popular aquatic centre in Melbourne rocked by alleged changeroom filming incident: 'Deeply concerned'

Police attended Brimbank Aquatic and Wellness Centre in Keilor Downs within minutes of the alleged incident being reported shortly after 11am on Sunday.

Actual Article Body:
By KYLIE STEVENS, SENIOR BREAKING NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  20:00 AEDT, 27 October 2026   |  Updated:  20:01 AEDT, 27 October 2026

A man has been banned from a Melbourne aquatic centre and charged by police after he was allegedly caught secretly filming several patrons inside a family changing room cubicle.

Police attended Brimbank Aquatic and Wellness Centre in Keilor Downs within five minutes of the alleged incident being reported shortly after 11am on Sunday.

A patron attending the facility with his wife and young children raised the alarm after he allegedly noticed a phone recording from under a gap while in the changing room.

It is alleged the man deleted the video and threw the phone in a nearby bin when confronted.

The device was retrieved by a pool lifeguard before police allegedly located the footage in the phone's 'recently deleted' folder, The Age reported.

A Caroline Springs man, 62, was arrested and has since been charged with one count of producing child abuse material and one count of producing intimate images.

He was bailed to appear in Sunshine Magistrates' Court on March 23.

Victoria Police confirmed to the Daily Mail on Tuesday that the investigation is ongoing and have not ruled out additional charges.

A man has been charged after he was allegedly caught illegally filming several patrons inside a a family changing room at Brimbank Aquatic and Wellness Centre (pictured)

Police investigations into the alleged incident continue

'Police are working with the aquatic centre,' a spokeswoman said.

'Police are in the process of contacting those potentially impacted by the alleged offending and expect to identify further alleged victims.'

'Working through this process is expected to take some time. As the investigation remains ongoing, further updates will be provided when appropriate.

'We absolutely understand how concerning this is for the community and the community should be rest assured police are conducting a full and thorough investigation.'

Brimbank Council, which operates the facility, has since addressed the alleged incident, adding that the man's membership from all of its leisure centres has been terminated.

'Brimbank Council is deeply concerned by an alleged incident involving the unsolicited and illegal use of recording device within a changeroom at the Brimbank Aquatic and Wellness Centre, on Sunday October 25,' a statement read

'Our thoughts are with the individual and family directly affected, and we acknowledge the distress this incident may have caused others in our community.

'The safety and wellbeing of our community and all visitors to our facilities remains our highest priority.

The man has been banned from the aquatic centre (pictured) and all other Brimbank Council-run leisure centres

Police investigations into Sunday's alleged incident at the facility continue

'We understand that this incident may cause concern among families and members of our community, and we want to reassure residents that council takes these matters extremely seriously.'

The council added that it continues to work closely with police regarding the investigation.

It's understood that a safety review of changerooms will also be conducted.

Opened in 2022, Brimbank Aquatic and Wellness Centre attracts more than 1.5 million visitors every year.

Anyone with more information or who was at the aquatic centre at 11am on Sunday is urged to call Crime Stoppers.
